preconditions.description: The number of students n is between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= f_i <= n and f_i != i and 1 <= s_i <= 2 for i in range(1, n+1) for f_i, s_i in [input_lines[i-1].split()])
preconditions.description: For each student i (1-based), their best friend f_i is a valid student (1 ≤ f_i ≤ n, f_i ≠ i) and their sex s_i is either 1 (boy) or 2 (girl).
The input contains exactly n lines of student data after the first line.

postconditions.description: t is the maximum number of valid pairs (student and their best friend) that can be formed without overlapping students, and e is the maximum number of boy-girl pairs among all such solutions.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n and 1 <= b_i <= n and (a_i == f_b_i or b_i == f_a_i) for a_i, b_i in pairs)
postconditions.description: Each pair (a_i, b_i) consists of two students where one is the best friend of the other, and all students in the pairs are distinct.
The number of pairs printed equals t.
No student is included in more than one pair.

postconditions.expression: e == sum(1 for a_i, b_i in pairs if (s_a_i == 1 and s_b_i == 2) or (s_a_i == 2 and s_b_i == 1))
postconditions.description: e is the count of boy-girl pairs in the solution.
